scope: Manual archive-pinned comparison of all twelve remaining interfaces from aos-2024-v52-i02-p0466, preserving the frozen source conventions for oblique trees and local variation.

rows.query: Uniform conditional shifted exponential-power response tail bound; bounded conditional-tail/sub-Weibull search and inspection of conditional distribution, exponential and real-power definitions.
rows.result: A chosen real-response conditional kernel can evaluate the event |y|>B+M at each covariate, and real arithmetic expresses the displayed uniform bound with positive constants.
rows.gap: The assumption is expressible using a chosen conditional-law version and exponential-power inequalities, with pointwise uniformity stronger than the kernel's almost-everywhere identification.

comparisons.D10: Use a single c1,c2,gamma,M>0 for all x in X and all B>=0, with the strict event |y|>B+M. The tail is for the uncentered conditional response, not its regression residual or a marginal response law. A condDistrib version only has its statistical identity almost everywhere, so the asserted bound at every covariate is an explicit version-dependent assumption. Keep finite positive real gamma in this formula; the separate source convention gamma=infinity for bounded data has undefined boundary powers and is not an instance of Real.rpow. The tail shift M and threshold B are distinct from ridge term counts and forest tree counts.

rows.query: Terminal-node sample-average regression tree prediction; inspected filtering finite observation indices and pointwise finite sums.
rows.result: Filter indices by covariate membership in the terminal cell, count them, and divide their response sum by that count to define the leaf mean and its piecewise-constant prediction.
rows.gap: Finite filtering and averaging support prediction once the terminal-cell routing and nonempty-node domain are specified.

comparisons.D5: For x in terminal cell t return sum_{i:x_i in t} y_i divided by n(t), retaining repeated observations through their indices. This is a node mean, not a sum normalized by the full sample size or a population conditional mean. Require n(t)>0 and unique routing through the split boundary conventions; the source does not give an empty-leaf fallback. The announced general finite-dictionary least-squares extension is not substituted for this canonical output.

rows.query: CART oblique split decrease in sum-of-squares error with global sample normalization; inspected finite dot product, real indicators and finite sums.
rows.result: The two residual sums and halfspace routing indicators directly define the split score for admissible splits whose parent and child means are defined.
rows.gap: The score is definable by these ingredients on a nonempty-child domain, while the source's unrestricted split optimization still needs empty-child conventions.

comparisons.D2: Use 1/n in both parent and split residual sums, not 1/n(t). Sum over the parent observations, replacing the parent mean by ybar_left*1(a dot x_i<=b)+ybar_right*1(a dot x_i>b) in the second residual. The left equality and right strict inequality allocate the boundary once. Means require their own node counts; totalized real division at an empty child would invent a source convention. Maximizing this score is the later split-selection problem, not an identity proved by the finite-sum ingredients.

rows.query: Sparse randomized candidate directions and probability of multiplicative split-score success; inspected coordinate support counts, finite-image maximum attainment and data-conditional laws.
rows.result: Coordinate counts encode direction sparsity, and a finite nonempty set of attainable split scores has a maximum even when the parameter set is infinite. A conditional law of the search mechanism describes the success event once its maxima and measurability are established.
rows.gap: The remaining interface supplies admissible candidate splits, measurable maximizing values and their data-conditional success probability, resolving empty-child and candidate-nonemptiness conventions.

comparisons.D3: Bound the number of nonzero coordinates of every a in A_t by the positive integer d, without adding d<=p. Compare the candidate maximum over real b and a in A_t to kappa times the unrestricted maximum, where 0<kappa<=1. The probability is over search-space randomness conditional on the data, not an unconditional data probability or a ratio of expected scores. The finite-values argument can use Finset.exists_max_image after constructing a nonempty finite image of a well-defined score and lifting a maximizing value to a parameter; it does not resolve undefined empty-child means, empty candidates or tie selection. Preserve the source's displayed count bound as source wording rather than deriving a different partition count.

rows.query: Greedy maximal oblique decision tree with depth and data-degeneracy stopping; bounded regression-tree search and inspection of binary-tree constructors, hyperplane score and maximum predicate.
rows.result: BinaryTree supplies a finite recursive shape and real halfspaces supply child regions. Statistical node labels, valid split selection, prediction routing and the exact stopping tests must be implemented on top of that structure.
rows.gap: The remaining construction adds data-bearing cells, admissible greedy splits, stopping and measurable selection to a binary tree, preserving the source's degeneracy conventions.

comparisons.D4: Split a parent into its intersection with a dot x<=b and a dot x>b using the selected parameters, then recurse up to K levels unless there is one observation or all input values and/or all response values agree as printed. T_K may stop before depth K and T_max is the maximally grown stopped tree, not a complete tree with exactly 2^K leaves. BinaryTree stores labels in node constructors and uses nil for empty branches, so terminal-cell labels require an explicit representation convention. IsMaxOn omits feasible membership and a selector, and does not resolve the source's empty-child or tie ambiguities.

rows.query: Total variation of univariate ridge profiles on projected node intervals and finite additive variation cost; inspected extended variation's monotone finite-sequence supremum and bounded-variation predicate.
rows.result: For a specified real interval, eVariationOn represents the supremum of absolute successive profile increments and retains infinite values. Finite sums give a representation-dependent additive variation cost, while endpoint conventions and derivative-integral identities need additional work.
rows.gap: The remaining comparison resolves the source's projected endpoints and partition indexing and distinguishes representation variation from a norm or an automatically valid derivative-integral formula.

comparisons.D6: Apply variation to the univariate profile h on the projection interval I(a,t), not to a signed measure or to the multivariate function with a coordinatewise variation norm. On a finite closed interval, endpoint-inclusive partition sums can be compared to eVariationOn's finite monotone sequences; the source uses min/max for possibly open or unbounded cells and allows infinite endpoints without defining h there. Retain those unresolved conventions and the |P| versus |P|+1 indexing discrepancy. Sum the profile variations for the supplied finite representation, preserving the source's unbound-direction notation issue. Constants have zero variation, so calling this a norm needs a quotient or normalization not present in the source. The smooth integral representation requires an appropriate regularity and integrability theorem and is not supplied merely by BoundedVariationOn.

rows.query: Finite library of sums of ridge profiles with finite total variation cost; inspected finite linear predictors, sums and extended profile variation.
rows.result: A finite family of directions and univariate profiles determines each ridge sum, and a finite extended variation cost expresses the library restriction once the source interval conventions are fixed.
rows.gap: The finite ridge library can be constructed from these ingredients after specifying the representation and projection-interval variation conventions.

comparisons.D7: Allow arbitrary real directions and real univariate profiles, with a finite term count M>=1 and g(x)=sum_k g_k(a_k dot x). Do not restrict profiles to a fixed neural-network activation or impose a separate coefficient vector absent from the source. Membership requires a finite source variation cost for a representation; it is distinct from membership in the subsequent L2 closure and from finiteness of the relaxed local functional for every closure member. Keep this M separate from the positive response-tail shift constant.

rows.query: L2 closure of finite ridge library and epsilon-relaxed local total variation functional; inspected topological closure, L2 seminorm, extended variation and one-sided filter limits.
rows.result: Closure in an L2 topology and the approximation constraint are available, while extended infima of representation costs and an epsilon-downarrow-zero limit describe the relaxation without discarding infinity.
rows.gap: The remaining interface constructs the relaxed representation cost in the chosen L2 space and resolves the source's representative, interval and seminorm conventions.

comparisons.D8: First form F as the closure of G in L2(P_x), then for each epsilon>0 infimize the sum of node-local ridge variations over finite representations g with population L2 distance ||f-g||<=epsilon, and take the right-hand limit at zero. The approximating norm is not the empirical norm and the cost is local to t, with the global shorthand obtained at t=X. Use extended nonnegative values so an empty approximation family or unbounded costs are not silently converted to zero. An L2 equivalence class does not specify all pointwise representatives used in profile variation, and constants remain in the zero-cost kernel; neither representative choice nor a genuine norm structure is settled by closure.

rows.query: Pruned rooted binary subtree and penalized least-squares smallest minimizer; bounded cost-complexity/regression-tree search and inspection of binary-tree structure and set-constrained minimizer predicate.
rows.result: The optimization predicate can represent empirical squared error plus lambda times the terminal-node count over a supplied pruning relation. Neither a rooted contraction relation nor the smallest-minimizer theorem follows from the generic binary-tree type.
rows.gap: The remaining interface implements rooted pruning and the penalized minimizer and addresses the source's overbroad smallest-subtree comparison and inconsistent weakest-link prose.

comparisons.D9: Pruning repeatedly collapses internal splits while preserving the root, and |T| counts terminal cells rather than all nodes. Minimize the empirical loss (1/n)*sum_i(y_i-mu-hat(T)(x_i))^2 plus lambda_n*|T| with lambda_n>=0, requiring feasible-tree membership in addition to IsMinOn. A finite pruning family supports attainment but does not alone prove a unique least minimizing tree. The printed explanation compares T_opt to every pruned subtree, not only other minimizers; retain that discrepancy rather than silently correcting it. The separate prose about collapsing nodes decreasing unpenalized least-squares error is not a verified algorithm for this objective.

rows.query: Uniform-depth expected sum of q-th powers of terminal-node local variation; inspected nonnegative integration and real powers with q>2.
rows.result: Given the local variation functional and random tree, sum its q-th powers over terminal nodes and integrate under the joint data/search law. The displayed bound is an explicit assumption with the same q at every depth.
rows.gap: The assumption is expressible once local variation and measurable random terminal-node sums are supplied, retaining extended values until their finite bound is established.

comparisons.D11: Require mu in F and positive V with a common q>2 such that E[sum_{t in T_K} ||mu||_{L1(t)}^q]<=V^q for every K>=1. Here t in T_K denotes terminal nodes and the expectation includes data and search-space randomness. Do not replace the aggregate q-power sum by the q-th power of a global variation or choose a new q for each depth. The source allows sample-size dependence of V in its later discussion; the uniform-depth quantifier remains. Infinite local variation cannot be made finite by converting an extended value to a real number.

rows.query: Moment bound for the largest terminal-node occupancy at every tree depth; inspected finite maxima, nonnegative moments and real powers and compared the saved stopping-rule inconsistency.
rows.result: Finite maxima of leaf counts and a nu-th moment express the left side. The literal all-depth bound is problematic for a fixed nonempty finite sample whose tree stops, because that maximum stays at least one while A*n/2^K tends to zero.
rows.gap: The moment expression is supported, but the source's unlimited-depth quantifier must be clarified to obtain a satisfiable bound for the stated stopped-tree family.

comparisons.D12: Use the same q>2 from D11 and nu>=1+2/(q-2), take the maximum of n(t) over terminal cells, then its nu-th power, expectation under the joint data/search law and the 1/nu power; the right side is A*n/2^K. A may depend on n but is fixed across K at a given n. For nonempty samples the largest leaf has at least one observation even after stopping, contradicting the right side for sufficiently large K with finite A. Preserve and flag the literal for-all-K>=1 statement; do not restrict K to feasible depths or impose complete balanced trees as an unprinted repair.

rows.query: Oblique random forest using size-N subsampling without replacement and independent randomization copies; bounded random-forest search and inspection of fixed-cardinality subsets, finite product laws and finite prediction averages.
rows.result: Fixed-cardinality subsets describe allowable subsamples, and a product law can supply independent randomization copies for fixed training data. Averaging their supplied tree predictors yields the forest; the actual subsampling and candidate-direction laws remain inputs.
rows.gap: The remaining procedure supplies the conditional randomization law and tree builder, preserving sampling without replacement and the shared-data dependence of predictions.

comparisons.D13: Theta includes a size-N subset of the n training indices without replacement and the random candidate directions at each tree node. The source does not specify a uniform subsampling law or uniquely select one of the purely random direction examples, so powersetCard describes admissible subsets without supplying a probability distribution. Use B independent copies of the mechanism conditional on the shared original data, train depth-K stopped trees on those subsamples and average predictions with 1/B for B>0. Do not assert unconditional independence of predictions, replace subsampling by bootstrap sampling with replacement, or replace N by n in the forest theorem's effective sample size and subsample expectation.
